book: Campaign ads, donor PACs, and staged outrage marketed with the calm discipline of a launch deck.
A brain device pitched to an exhausted public as mercy while turning memory itself into infrastructure.
Billionaire Dijon Garnier does not need the podium. He finances the corridors surrounding it.
world: Darnell Covington enters the story with a mind sharp enough to open doors and a country eager to decide what that mind is for.
Javon reads people faster than Darnell reads systems. Their friendship becomes one of the few records the machine cannot rewrite.
Garnier does not need to rule in public. He buys routes, installs dependencies, and lets institutions call the result stability.
Alec moves through the intelligence layer where surveillance, duty, and dark comedy collide.
The technology layer turns forgetting into convenience and correction into a civic service with a clean interface.
The title starts as an insult and becomes a structure: people failing upward while everyone below inherits the invoice.
reader: What does the title make you expect about power, competence, and blame?
How does Darnell’s promise become a trap before he names the system?
Where does patriotism stop being language and start becoming coercion?
What kind of victory is possible after memory itself becomes contested?
facts: Satirical political thriller, dark political fiction, and coming of age novel
Manuscript in active revision; the author is writing the climax. The reader list is open for early readers, reviewers, podcasters, and booksellers.
A brilliant young man enters a country where donor money, draft pressure, surveillance language, and public incompetence keep tightening around him.
press: The Ironic Ineptocracy is a satirical political thriller about brilliance, friendship, private money, public failure, and the machinery that turns incompetence into authority.

Darnell Covington can see the life he wants. Javon Whitfield sees danger gathering around the room. Dijon Garnier sees a country that can be bought, routed, and corrected. The novel follows the pressure as ambition becomes evidence and the official story keeps changing.
dispatches: The title sounds like a joke until the file starts reading like a diagnosis.
The machine does not ask who is guilty. It asks who can be processed.
Power does not only want the event. It wants the version of the event people are allowed to keep.
Garnier does not need the throne. He owns the room around it.
dossier: Power rarely arrives under its own name. It arrives as funding, access, convenience, policy, and memory.
